# Draft:Battle of Bujan

The Battle of Bujan was a military engagement fought between Albanian partisans and local resistance fighters against Yugoslav Partisan forces in Bujan, Kosovo during December 1944 – January 1945. Albanian forces temporarily resisted Yugoslav attempts to take control of the region.
Background
During the final stages of World War II, Albanian forces in Kosovo resisted both Axis occupation and the advancing Yugoslav Partisans. Local leaders organized defenses to maintain control of key areas, including the strategic town of Bujan.
Battle
Yugoslav Partisan units advanced on Bujan with the goal of securing the region. Albanian resistance fighters, familiar with the terrain, conducted defensive operations, ambushes, and hit-and-run tactics. The Albanian forces were able to temporarily repel the Yugoslav units.
Outcome
The battle concluded with an Albanian resistance victory in the short term, as they retained control of Bujan for several weeks. Eventually, political and military developments in the region shifted control, but the battle became a symbol of Albanian resistance during the period.
